newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria holds, Nigeria hit in Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria holds, Nigeria hit in Brady market.

text.p: Bulgaria Bradys managed to hold up on Tuesday after their battering the previous day, while Nigeria was knocked down by what appeared to be a single seller.
But the rest of the market, worried that U.S. interest rates might rise, was largely on hold, keeping an eye on U.S. data this week, especially Friday's payroll figures for December.
One trader said there was a slightly better bid to Bulgarian bonds this morning, its high yield continuing to attract some buying at the lower levels.

"It's only for the very brave. It will be difficult to implement a currency board, and there are all the problems with the government and social unrest. It's got high yield but can you live with the constant worry," he added.
However, the market still expects the Bulgarian government to avoid default and meet its debt repayments later this month.
Russia, with the holiday there keeping trade thin, was holding steady after Monday's dip on fresh concerns over President Boris Yeltsin's health.
But traders said Russian paper -- Vneshekonombank dollar debt is hovering just under 80 cents in the dollar -- still looked to be good value.
An International Monetary Fund team returns to Moscow next week for talks and monetary sources in Washington said both sides were hopeful that the organisation would approve further loans to Russia.
About the biggest move of the morning was in Nigerian pars which dropped around 1/2 a point on what one trader said was a sale of some $25 million.
There was another bomb blast in Lagos on Tuesday, but traders said the sale was more likely triggered by profit-taking.
Nigerian bonds reached an all-time high of 69 cents in the dollar at the end of December, a rise of some 44 percent since the start of 1996.
